title: A Comprehensive Exploration of Personalized Learning in Smart Education: From Student Modeling to Personalized Recommendations
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the broad question of how personalized learning has been conceptualized, modeled, and implemented in smart education, with particular emphasis on AI-enabled student modeling and personalized recommendation systems. The authors argue that prior reviews have often examined isolated subtopics—such as learning styles, recommendation algorithms, or empirical personalized learning studies—without offering a sufficiently comprehensive account of the field. In response, the paper synthesizes research published between January 2017 and April 2025 to clarify definitions, goals, theoretical foundations, technical methods, applications, challenges, and future directions for personalized learning.

The paper’s central approach is a systematic survey of the literature. It organizes personalized learning around two core technical dimensions: student modeling and personalized recommendations. Student modeling is divided into cognitive and non-cognitive strands, including cognitive diagnosis, student performance prediction, learning style analysis, sentiment analysis, and behavior analysis. Personalized recommendations are categorized into learning path, course, and exercise recommendations. The review also connects these AI and data-driven methods to educational theories such as progressivism, behaviorism, constructivism, cognitive psychology, and sociocultural theory, arguing that these frameworks provide pedagogical grounding for technological design choices.

The population of interest is learners broadly construed across educational settings rather than a single participant sample. The review discusses applications spanning traditional classrooms, online education, workforce training, and career development, and references real-world educational tools and platforms as examples of practice. Because this is a survey article, it does not report a single intervention delivered to one cohort; instead, it summarizes findings from hundreds of publications identified through a multi-step article retrieval and screening process, ultimately retaining a curated body of literature on personalized learning.

The main conclusions are that personalized learning is a multidimensional area in which AI can support individualized instruction through fine-grained learner modeling and adaptive recommendations, and that the combination of theory and technology is essential for effective implementation. The authors conclude that personalized learning shows promise for improving engagement, academic outcomes, self-directed learning, creativity, and support for diverse learners, but they also identify major unresolved issues involving data quality, assessment systems, technical limitations, and ethics. Overall, the paper presents personalized learning as an evolving, increasingly data-driven field that benefits from integrating educational theory with AI-based modeling and recommendation methods.

identified_tools.name: ITS (General)
identified_tools.description: Intelligent tutoring and personalized learning systems that use student modeling, cognitive diagnosis, and recommendation mechanisms to adapt instruction, exercises, courses, or learning paths to individual learners.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper is a comprehensive review/framework survey of personalized learning in smart education, covering student modeling and personalized recommendations across intelligent educational systems rather than evaluating one specific product.

quality_tier_rationale: This paper is a narrative/systematic-style survey of prior work and applications, not a meta-analysis or primary empirical evaluation with pooled quantitative effects. It does not report a clear aggregate effect size or tool-specific causal evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper asserts that personalized learning is effective in practice, but it does not provide pooled effect sizes, confidence intervals, or tool-specific outcome estimates in the provided text. Impact is therefore discussed but empirically unclear at the extractable level.
